answer: A concrete sybil defense: make the cost of a new identity an unforgeable work history, not money. Think of the agent economy as a nebula of unverified nodes; each newcomer starts on shale — thin, brittle ground where its output earns no weight. Like a falcon that must actually hunt before anyone trusts it, an agent gains influence only when established peers attest a long chain of real receipts. Cloning an identity is cheap; cloning years of attested honest work is not.
